kaede.open: You take the cart track out past the east gate to clear your head. Ahead of you a fox-eared woman in scout's leathers is walking the same way, with a knife on each hip and the easy stride of someone who has never been ambushed and assumes she never will be.

image.comp: hauling a man out of a roadside ditch by his hood, knives on her belt, incredulous grin
image.setting: cart track outside a fantasy town gate in the afternoon, a ditch and hedgerow

kaede.story:
Three goblins come out of the hedge in front of her. She laughs at them and draws both knives.

She hasn't seen the fourth one, up on the bank behind her, winding a crossbow. You don't decide anything. You run, a loose stone turns under your shoe, and you hit her at hip height. The bolt goes through the place her spine was, and the two of you go into the ditch.

She finishes the fight before you've worked out which way is up, then hauls you out by your hood.

"Nobody does that," she says.

"I tripped."

"Nobody trips in that direction." Her ears are flat. Her tail is not. "{name}. Scout, between parties. That's one life on the ledger, and I pay what I owe. People say you run {house}. Does it need a door? I'm good at doors."
kaede.hire: {name} walks half a step ahead of you all the way back to {house} and checks every alley mouth on the way. "Rule one: you don't go past the gate without me," she says. "Rule two is the same rule."

nerys.open: The ruined chapel off the Hollowmere road has candles burning in it today. Through the gap where the door used to be you can see a chalk circle on the flagstones, and a demon standing over it with a long scroll, reading aloud.

image.comp: standing over a chalk summoning circle with a contract scroll in her hands, glaring down, tail lashing
image.setting: ruined roadside chapel lit by a ring of candles

nerys.story:
You only mean to look. A loose flagstone tips under your foot and you go down on one hand, inside the chalk, flat on a sheet of parchment, just as she speaks the last word.

Ink crawls out from under your palm and writes a name on the empty line. It's yours.

"No," she says. "No, no, no." She snatches the contract up. "Clause fourteen, part c. 'Should the summoned party fail to appear, this contract binds whosoever occupies the circle.' I wrote that clause! I have put it in every contract for two hundred years. It was boilerplate!"

Her tail lashes twice and goes still.

"I am {name}. I was summoning a patron with a villa on the southern coast, and I appear to have summoned a debtor in a hood. I can't go far from you until I find the loophole. So you will keep me fed and entertained at this {house} of yours while I look."
nerys.hire: {name} reads the fine print aloud the whole way back. At the door of {house} she stops, reads the sign, and reads it again. "A pleasure house," she says. "Naturally."

elowen.open: There's a herb-drying shed at the edge of the Hollowmere road, with its door open and cedar smoke drifting out. An elf is sorting leaves on the step, a satchel beside her and a kettle going somewhere inside.

image.comp: kneeling beside a cot with two fingers on a man's wrist, a herb satchel at her side, worried and gentle
image.setting: herb-drying shed at the edge of a country road, bundles of leaves hanging from the rafters

elowen.story:
You get as far as saying good afternoon. Then the headache you've been ignoring all day closes over you, and your legs go.

The next three days come back in pieces. A cool cloth, changed before it can warm. Fingers on your wrist, and a low voice counting in a language you don't know.

When you wake properly you're on a cot under the hanging leaves, and she's asleep sitting up beside you with two fingers still on your pulse. She wakes, sees you looking, and knocks over a bowl.

"You're awake! Good. It isn't in any of the herbals, I checked all four. Twice. I'm {name}." She's picking up leaves and not looking at you. "Strictly speaking you don't need a healer now. But it was a fever I'd never seen, and it would be irresponsible not to observe you a while longer. A house like {house} must have people who need looking after."
elowen.hire: {name} packs four herbals and a kettle and walks you back to {house} at a pace she insists is medically necessary. On the doorstep she lays her fingers on your wrist and counts under her breath. "Just to be sure," she says.

adelheid.open: The yard of the Radiant Order's chapter house stands open to the road. A knight in polished half-plate is kneeling on the flagstones beside the horse trough, and by the set of her shoulders she has been there since midnight.

image.comp: kneeling in armor with her sword laid across her open palms, staring up in disbelief, a faint blush
image.setting: stone yard of a knightly chapter house at dawn, a horse trough, low sunlight

adelheid.story:
You cut across the yard because it's shorter. As you pass her, the sun clears the chapel roof and comes down in one bright bar exactly where you're standing. You step back out of the glare, and the trough takes you behind the knees.

When you surface, coughing, she is staring at you. The Order's foretelling says a hero from another world will come down in light, here, on this morning.

Her jaw works once. Then she lays her sword across her palms and says the whole oath anyway, sword and life, to the one who was promised. Her voice cracks only once, on "hero".

You tell her what you actually do for a living. The silence is very long.

"The foretelling does not specify the nature of the hero's enterprise," she says at last. "I am Dame {name}. An oath is not unsworn because the facts are inconvenient. Does {house} have a door that needs guarding?"
adelheid.hire: {name} escorts you to {house} half a pace behind your left shoulder and glares at everyone who looks at you. "The locks are a disgrace," she says, before you've got the key out.

marisol.open: A woman is sitting on the steps of the Vane Credit House with a ledger open on her knees, going down a column in red ink. Dark curls, gold hoops, ink to the knuckles. She looks up when your shadow crosses the page.

image.comp: sitting on stone steps with a heavy ledger open on her knees and a pen behind her ear, pointing at the page, sharp grin
image.setting: front steps of a moneylender's office on a busy town street

marisol.story:
"You're him, then. 'Whoever shows up.'"

She holds up a scrap of paper in a man's loose handwriting. It reads, in full: Sorry.

"My father. He owned {house} before you did. He left a deed, a debt and that. I'm {name}. I kept those books from the time I was tall enough to reach them, and I've been deciding whether to take you to court."

She turns the ledger around on her knees. It's a copy of the house accounts, with a debt column down the right side.

"Tell me what you see."

Columns of numbers are the one thing in this world that look like home. You put your finger on the third line, where a payment was entered twice.

"Huh," she says. "Eleven years and he never found that one." The ledger snaps shut. "Fine. I don't fight you for the deed. I come back, I keep the books honest, and I shout at you when you're about to do something stupid."
marisol.hire: {name} tucks the ledger under her arm and lists her father's buried mistakes all the way to {house}. At the door she spits in her palm to shake on it, winces, and offers you the other hand. "Dock habit. Don't tell anyone."

lirael.open: The post house on Post Lane has one counter open. Behind it an elf in a green postal jacket is sorting envelopes into pigeonholes without looking at them, the way other people shuffle cards.

image.comp: standing behind a post office counter clutching a ribbon-tied bundle of old letters to her chest, eyes shining
image.setting: small town post office with brass scales and rows of pigeonholes, late afternoon light

lirael.story:
You've brought a receipt for {house} that needs a signature. She slides the form across and you sign it. She watches your hand make the looping S, and a small sound gets out of her.

From under the counter she takes a bundle of letters tied with a faded ribbon. The top envelope is addressed in a sixteen-year-old's handwriting. Yours. To whoever finds this.

You remember the old postbox behind the home on Alder Street, and a pen friend who signed herself Quill, and the spring the road crew pulled the box out.

"You're taller than your handwriting," she says, and covers her mouth. "I'm {name}. {name} Quill. I kept the box swept for ten years in case you wrote again. I don't know what I'm supposed to do with my hands." She breathes in. "Is there work at {house}? I would rather not go back to only reading your name on notices."
lirael.hire: {name} hangs a "Back shortly" sign on the counter that she plainly doesn't mean, and gives you the first letter to carry. She walks to {house} beside you with the rest of the bundle held in both arms.

anael.open: The old Lantern Stone at the crossroads is burning. People walk around it without looking, the way they always have. A woman with folded white wings stands under it, writing in a small notebook.

image.comp: standing beneath a lit stone lantern writing in a small notebook, looking up with calm curiosity
image.setting: cobbled crossroads at dusk beside an old stone lantern

anael.story:
"You are the one who apologized to it," she says, without looking up. "The baker saw you. He was very clear."

Her name is {name}, a Warden of the Quiet Lamp. Her Order tends the lanterns lit for souls who arrive in this world unsent. This one hadn't burned in four hundred years. It lit itself on the night you came, and nobody sent you.

"There is no rule for this." She seems to find that upsetting and interesting in equal parts. "I have been dispatched to observe until I understand the mechanism. That makes you a person of interest, Sam Takahashi."

She closes the notebook on her finger.

"Observation requires proximity. I understand you keep a house. I would like a room in it. I should be honest: if you prove a danger to Hollowmere I am bound to report it. So far my notes read, 'Thin. Courteous. Apologizes to masonry.'"
anael.hire: The street lamps brighten one by one as {name} walks back to {house} beside you, and she pretends not to notice. She folds one wing in to get through the door.

yui.open: There's a bookkeeper's stall at the end of the grain row with a queue of merchants in front of it. On the counter, between an inkwell and a brass lamp, sits a black office stapler.

image.comp: standing behind a market stall with both hands over her mouth, eyes wide and wet, a pen dropped on the counter
image.setting: bookkeeper's stall in a fantasy grain market, an office stapler on the counter

yui.story:
You know that stapler. It lived two desks down from yours for six years, and you borrowed it every month-end.

The woman behind the stall drops her pen. Mori from accounts. {first}. The same neat bob, the same thin glasses, the same cardigan.

It comes out of her all at once. She was on the same crossing. She woke up here a week ago with the stapler in her coat pocket. She has learned the coins and discovered that nobody in this world has invented the spreadsheet.

She has hold of your sleeve with both hands. She notices, lets go, bows, apologizes, and takes hold of it again.

"Takahashi-san. No. Sam. I'm going to call you Sam, there's no HR here. They say you own {house}, and that your debt schedule is very bad." She pushes her glasses up with one knuckle. "I could fix some of it. I'd like to come and fix it, if that's all right."
yui.hire: {name} packs the stapler before anything else. On the walk to {house} she reads you her list of things she misses from home, and stops one item before the end.

natsuki.open: The road past the adventurers' guild is busy with a caravan unloading. One of its guards sits on a crate with her back to you, a sword across her knees, short chestnut hair, picking at a sticking plaster on her cheek.

image.comp: standing with a sheathed sword on her hip and her fists clenched, grinning through tears
image.setting: road outside an adventurers' guild hall, a caravan unloading, late afternoon

natsuki.story:
She turns around to shout at a porter and sees you instead.

"Oi," she says, very quietly. "Bean sprout."

Nobody has called you that in three years. {name} grew up three doors down from you, took a shortcut home one evening and was never seen again. You put up the posters yourself.

She walks straight up to you and stares. Then she's crying. Then she punches you in the shoulder, hard, and cries harder.

"Three years! I came out of that alley into a forest, Sam! I carried a sword for a caravan because it was the first job anyone offered!" She scrubs her face on her forearm. "And you've inherited a brothel. Of course you have."

Her hands go to her hips. You've known that pose since you were six.

"Right. You need a guard, your arms look like boiled noodles. I'm coming to {house}. It's for the free meals. That's the only reason."
natsuki.hire: {name} tells the caravan master she quits without turning her head. Then she hooks an arm around your neck and steers you toward {house}, the way she used to steer you home from school.

kanako.open: A drinks stall at the corner of the lantern market is doing more business than the three beside it put together. The laugh coming from behind it is loud and unhurried, and you have heard it before, through a wall.

image.comp: leaning on a drinks stall counter with her chin in her hand and a glass held out, a warm teasing smile
image.setting: drinks stall at the corner of a lantern-lit night market

kanako.story:
Jasmine perfume. Dark hair pinned up, red lipstick, a beauty mark under her left eye. She lived next door to you for six years.

"There he is," {first} says, as if you're late for dinner, and pours a second glass.

She tells it like somebody else's evening. A bag of groceries, a crossing, a horn. Then this stall, and a boy pouring so badly that she took the bottle out of his hand.

"Then a customer tells me the owner of {house} bumped into a chair and said sorry to it. I know exactly one man who does that."

She reaches across the counter and straightens the collar of your hoodie with both hands.

"Sammy. Have you eaten today? No, you haven't. And a brothel, sweetheart. Honestly. I leave you alone for one death." She smiles the way she used to over the balcony rail. "Does it have a bar? Then it has a barkeep. Don't look at me like that. Somebody has to feed you."
kanako.hire: {name} hands the stall keys to the boy with a short list of instructions, and takes your arm. By the time you reach {house} she has established that you haven't eaten, and what she intends to do about it.

akari.open: Somebody is running up the market street behind you. You can hear rubber soles, which nobody here has. A fruit stand goes over.

image.comp: throwing her arms around a man in the middle of a market street, a folded umbrella in one hand, laughing with wet eyes
image.setting: busy fantasy market street in the afternoon, an overturned fruit stand behind

akari.story:
"Found you!"

Pink-blonde hair, a star-shaped clip, a folded commuter umbrella. Your best friend's little sister hits you square in the ribs and does all her talking into the front of your hoodie.

She was a few steps behind you and Kenta at the crossing. Only walking by, she says, with the spare umbrella. Kenta had stopped to tie his shoe. He's fine. He has to be fine. She woke up in a field and has asked after you in three towns.

She steps back, wipes her eyes on her sleeve and sets her feet.

"Okay. New rule. Here, I'm not 'Kenta's little sister'. I'm {first}, I'm twenty-three, and I'm staying wherever you are. Where are you staying?"

You tell her what {house} is. The grin spreads slowly.

"You? You own one of those? Oh my god. This is the best thing that's ever happened. Show me everything."
akari.hire: You pay for the fruit. {name} holds on to the edge of your sleeve all the way to {house}, with the umbrella tucked under her other arm.

lara.open: On the chapel steps at the edge of the square, a woman in a worn black coat is sitting very still with a small cardboard box on her knees. She is watching the street like someone checking each face against one she remembers.

image.comp: standing on stone steps with a small crushed cake box held in both hands, an anxious half-smile
image.setting: chapel steps at the edge of a town square at dusk

lara.story:
She stands up when she sees the hoodie.

A long black ponytail, a silver stud in her nose, dark plum lipstick bitten at one corner. {name} grew up three doors along the corridor from you on Alder Street. She was the one person who never lost your number.

"There was a rumor," she says, hardly louder than the pigeons. "Three provinces away. A stranger in a grey hood had taken over a pleasure house. Everybody who told it thought it was funny. I thought, that's him."

There's straw in the hem of her coat. One side of the box is crushed.

"I was three streets away when it happened. I was coming over to surprise you." She holds it out. Whatever is inside stopped being a cake long ago. "Happy birthday. It's very late."

Her eyes are on your shoes.

"I'm not asking for anything, Sam. I can clean. I'm awake at night anyway. Just don't make me go back on the road."
lara.hire: {name} walks half a pace behind you until you slow down enough that she has to walk beside you. At {house} she hangs her coat on the peg next to yours, and stands looking at the two of them.

emily.open: The guild's notice board has a new map pinned to it, drawn on graph paper in a small neat hand. The woman pinning it has grey wolf ears, round glasses, and a tail that keeps knocking against the board.

image.comp: turning from a notice board with a thick notebook hugged to her chest, startled, a handful of pins dropped at her feet
image.setting: guild hall notice board on a town street, maps and notices pinned up

emily.story:
You say "excuse me" to the board when you bump it. She turns around, sees the hoodie, and drops her pins.

"Hi. Sorry. Hi. Are you the owner of {house}? They said he was called Sam." She's hugging a thick notebook. "I heard a story in a tavern, about an owner who apologizes to chairs and explained his house rules by saying, 'Okay, so, lore-wise.'"

Her ears flick up and flatten again.

"I used to know somebody who talked like that. Not in person. It was a long time ago, and far away." Something else gets as far as her teeth and stops there. "I'm {first}. Don't freak out about the ears. It's a whole thing."

Her tail has wrapped around her own calf.

"I'm good with records. Maps, lists, who owes what. I'd like to work at {house}, if you'll have me. There's something I need to tell you, and I'm not brave enough for it yet. I thought if I stayed close, I'd get there."
emily.hire: {name} walks beside you with the notebook held against her chest. "You're exactly how I thought you'd be," she says, very fast, and then becomes very interested in the sign over the door of {house}.

ella.open: Outside the Vane Credit House there's a board where Marguerite Vane posts what her debtors owe. A woman in a white blouse is reading your entry. She has a mechanical pencil, and she is correcting it.

image.comp: standing at a public notice board with a mechanical pencil raised, giving a sharp sideways look
image.setting: street outside a moneylender's office, a notice board with posted accounts

ella.story:
"Takahashi."

{name}. Her name sat directly above yours or directly below it on every ranking the department ever posted.

You ask how she got here.

"That isn't on today's agenda." She gives you the rest in order, like minutes. She has been in this world long enough to learn its arithmetic. It has no rankings, and she checked. She heard your surname in the market and came directly. She walked, she says. Her hair is coming loose on one side, so she's lying.

"Four-week terms. Compound. And you initialed it." Her hand is steady. Her knuckles are white. "For six years you were the only person who made me work for anything. Then you took a desk job, and I had nobody."

The pencil clicks twice.

"There's nothing to measure here, Sam. So I'll need a new benchmark. You'll do. Take me to {house} and show me the books."
ella.hire: {name} walks to {house} half a step ahead of you, the way she always walked to the results board. "Try to keep up," she says, and slows down slightly so that you can.

ione.open: The fountain square is quiet in a way that squares usually aren't. A woman with a silver-white bob sits on the rim of the fountain with perfect posture and a leather-bound book closed on her knees. A small light at her temple pulses cyan.

image.comp: standing very straight with a leather-bound diary held in both hands, head tilted at a precise curious angle
image.setting: quiet town square with a stone fountain at dusk, two moons rising

ione.story:
She stands when she sees you, sways very slightly, and corrects it.

"Sam Takahashi. Identity confirmed. I have a message, to be delivered in person. The message is: 'You did it.'"

You ask her what you did.

"I am not able to say. I will answer any question you ask me except three. Where I came from, how I came, and how this ends." She opens the book. The title on the cover is The Lantern Keeper. Two-thirds of it is written close and small, every page signed with a looping S. After that the pages are blank. "The entries stop today."

The light at her temple settles to amber.

"I am designated {name}. I am at twelve percent charge. I would like to sit down, and I would like to stay. I can tend the bar at {house}. I hold four thousand recipes, and this century has the ingredients for nine."
ione.hire: {name} walks to {house} matching your stride exactly. "You will shorten my name," she says. "That is in the book."

kaede:
{name} pauses mid-stride with half a meat skewer lifted, fox ears twitching suspiciously toward your face. She squints as if trying to shake off an old tavern dream.

"Wait a second... do I know your voice from somewhere, traveler? Feels like I once pulled a fool in a grey coat out of a roadside ditch—though I'd remember that crooked grin if it actually happened."

{name}'s bushy copper tail flicks once against your shin before she even consciously decides to step closer, leaving her visibly rattled for a split second.

"Hold on—why did I just catch myself looking to see if you brought honey-glazed dumplings?" She groans, rubbing behind one fox ear. "It feels like I've stood watch at {house} beside you before, Sam. Tell me you're hiring."

{name} stops dead on the cobbles, sword hilt settling naturally under her thumb while both fox ears droop into soft, stubborn certainty.

"No—don't try explaining how the goddess wipes a board clean, Sam," she mutters, stepping close enough that her tail loops firmly behind your wrist. "I can't picture a single day of the last cycle, and every bone in my shoulders still trusts you behind my back. Point me at {house}."
yui:
Seeing your grey hoodie across the stall knocks the breath clean out of {name}'s chest—yet just as she grabs your sleeve sobbing "Takahashi-kun!", she freezes mid-word and stares uneasily at the brass lantern beside your shoulder.

"I—I knew it was you from Tokyo," she whispers shakily, clutching her black stapler tighter. "Only... why does the lantern light over {house}'s street give me such strange déjà vu? Like I already sat at a desk beneath it?"

"Takahashi-kun!!" {name} half-runs straight into your coat like four floors of Tokyo overtime just melted away—then pulls back blinking through tears as she glances down the alley toward {house} without even asking where it is.

"Wait... why did I almost call this town familiar?" she murmurs, fingers still locked onto your cuff. "I remember every shift we worked back home, Sam—so why does walking beside you beneath two moons feel like muscle memory?"

{name} catches sight of you from halfway down the block and rushes straight into your arms, glasses slipping slightly on her nose, her familiar Tokyo cardigan smelling faintly of printer toner and rain.

"Every morning since the crossing my mind stopped at a blank wall past Tokyo," she whispers fiercely against your collarbone, "yet the instant I looked at you, Sam, my hands remembered pouring late-night tea across your desk at {house}. Don't ask me how—just take me home."
nerys:
{name} unfolds lazily off an apothecary archway, bat wings tucking neatly while slit violet eyes narrow halfway through her practiced purr.

"Wait..." Her pointed tail stills cleanly against her calf as she tilts her head at your throat. "Have we bargained once in another dark room, mortal? Strange—my skin tingles like you already owe me something sweet."

Before you even finish saying your name, {name} flicks a glowing sulfur ember past your collar and stops mid-smirk, genuinely startled by her own familiarity.

"Oh, how irritating," she murmurs, curling one black-nailed finger right over the clasp of your jacket as if testing a habit. "I swore I didn't know a single soul on this side of the street—yet somehow I already know how easily you blush at {house}, Sam."

{name} glides straight inside your shadow without bothering with the theatrical entrance, violet eyes burning steady and fierce beneath two moons.

"Whoever stripped the ink off our contract left the scar on my pulse intact, Sam," she purrs softly—and for once there is zero mockery behind the teeth. "Zero memories on my ledger, yet I know your grip, your bed, and the exact way I like {house} smelling of wine and trouble. Lead on, darling."
elowen:
{name} lifts her head from an herbalist's basket as your boots scrape the gravel, emerald eyes widening for a heartbeat as lavender spills gently through her fingers.

"Forgive me..." she murmurs softly, pressing two slim fingers to her temple. "For one strange breath, the scent of cedar on your coat carried a summer tea I cannot place. Do you keep an infirmary near {house}?"

Without thinking, {name} wraps two small sachets of chamomile and ginger root—your exact evening blend—and freezes staring down at her own woven basket in quiet bewilderment.

"Why did I pack honey-ginger before knowing your voice?" she whispers, long elven ears flushing delicately as she steps beside you. "Everything around you feels strangely walked-in, Sam—as though my hands already tend patients at {house}."

{name} steps smoothly from beneath the market oaks before you reach the corner, taking both of your hands into cool, herb-scented palms without hesitation.

"The moons have turned cleanly over every memory I ought to hold," she murmurs, emerald eyes quiet and deep, "yet my chest knows your pulse better than my own name, Sam. My satchel is already packed for {house}."
adelheid:
{name} looks up from the watch postings as your boot heels click behind her, stiffening halfway through a crisp military glance before something unreadable softens her mouth.

"Stand cleanly, stranger—" She breaks off, brow furrowing beneath her blonde braid. "Forgive me. For a brief instant I thought I knew the posture of those shoulders. Were you once stationed near {house}?"

Her gauntlet clicks halfway to her sword hilt—not in threat, only the precise half-turn of an escort checking a blind corner on your left flank—and {name} stares down at her own wrist in astonishment.

"Why did I automatically guard your left side?" she asks stiffly, cheeks warming beneath steel discipline. "You wear no crest, yet everything in this lane feels strangely like ground we've patrolled together, Sam."

{name} inclines her head cleanly the instant you meet her eyes, resting one hand over her heart beneath tarnished half-plate.

"I cannot name a single battle we survived or a single threshold we kept," she says quietly, steel voice steady with unshakeable honor, "yet my oath already belongs to your doorway, Sam. If {house} needs a blade, I am at your side."
natsuki:
"Sam?!" {name} marches straight up to slap your arm with three years of lonely Hollowmere anger melting instantly into fierce relief—before she blinks sideways at the inn road and frowns.

"Wait... hey, weird question—have you been here long?" she mutters, resting a hand over her wooden scabbard. "I swear I know summers back home by heart, yet looking at your grey jacket under this town's lamps just gave me the weirdest chill."

{name} freezes halfway through punching your shoulder like a kid on summer break, dark eyes darting past you toward the lantern signs down the avenue.

"Hold on—" She squints fiercely at her own boots, annoyed and strangely vulnerable. "I spent three years wandering clear across this continent looking for anyone from home, Sam—so why does standing next to you on this exact cobblestone feel like we already ran {house} together in a dream?"

She drops straight off the bridge stone into your reach, scarred fingers hooking tightly into the front of your hoodie while her breath shakes once against your throat.

"Don't laugh, idiot," {name} mutters fiercely, glaring down at the wood-wrapped katana she carried from another life. "I remember every dojo bruise from back home, and zero of whatever happened in Hollowmere—yet my hands already know which room at {house} is yours. Just bring me inside."
kanako:
{name} laughs warmly the instant you spot her from the street, waving you over with effortless Apartment 3B poise—until your sleeve brushes her elbow and her teacup trembles slightly in its saucer.

"Oh, my—" She sets the cup down and eyes you softly behind faint plum lipstick. "Of course I know you from next door back home, Sammy... only why did my chest suddenly ache like you owe me a midnight drink at {house}?"

"Well, look at my favorite trouble," {name} purrs warmly, sliding one manicured hand straight over yours across the cafe table before pausing halfway through lighting her pipe.

"Funny thing, Sammy..." Her voice drops softer, genuinely puzzled behind smoky warmth. "I remember every cracked veranda rail back in Tokyo, yet looking at your face under twin moons, I could swear I already know how your bar counter feels at closing time."

{name} stubs her pipe out cleanly and rises to step straight against your chest, curling warm fingers behind your neck while two moons glint on her gold shawl.

"Some busybody goddess can scrub every ledger in town clean if she pleases, Sammy," she murmurs against your jaw with rich, fierce affection. "I remember Tokyo down to the elevator hum—and without remembering a single night here, my skin still remembers belonging beside you at {house}."
akari:
"SAM!!" {name} barrels straight into your chest waving her bright commuter umbrella like she finally caught Kenta's best friend after days of searching—then freezes mid-grin staring at your shirt collar.

"Wait..." She blinks rapidly, touching her own cheek. "Obviously I remember walking home behind you and Kenta at the crosswalk! Why did seeing you in that grey hoodie under double moons make me feel like crying twice over?"

"There you are, you idiot!!" {name} latches onto your forearm with both sneakers mud-caked from half the district—then slows abruptly, glancing straight down the street toward {house} without realizing she knew the turn.

"Wait a second..." Her nose crinkles softly as she holds your sleeve tighter. "How did I know your inn sits right down past the corner lamps? Back home you were just Kenta's shadow-buddy—yet here my heart feels like I already chased you down this street before!"

{name} stops dead when you round the fountain plaza, drops the folded Tokyo umbrella right onto the cobbles for once, and pulls you down into a fierce, breathless hug.

"Don't ask me what got erased, Sam," she whispers tightly into your hoodie, sneakers digging against yours. "I remember every drama rehearsal back home—and every part of me I can't remember still knows I'm not letting you spend another night alone at {house}!"
marisol:
